Class LogFormatter.Builder

java.lang.Object
io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogFormatter.Builder
Enclosing interface:
LogFormatter
public static final class LogFormatter.Builder extends Object
Log formatter builder that is composed of other formatters. The add(LogFormatter) are executed in insertion order. This builder is smart and will coalesce and consolidate formatters! For example if only formatter is added to the builder it will be returned instead of a new formatter.

    • keyValues

      public LogFormatter.Builder keyValues()
      Creates a formatter that will print ALL of the key values the same way Logback's %X/%mdc does: comma-space separated key=value pairs with no surrounding braces (unlike Log4j2, which wraps the same pairs in {}), and no percent encoding. An empty map renders as an empty string. Keys that are mapped to null will only have the key printed and no separating equal sign (=), to differentiate empty string and null. For the percent-encoded RFC 3986 URI query style instead, see encodedKeyValues().
      Returns:
      formatter.

    • keyValues

      public LogFormatter.Builder keyValues(List<String> keys)
      Creates a formatter that will print the key values in order of the passed in keys if they exist, Logback %X style (see keyValues() for the exact format). An empty list is considered a noop and no keys will be ommitted! If you want all keys use keyValues(). For the percent-encoded style instead, see encodedKeyValues(List).
      Parameters:
      keys - keys where order is important.
      Returns:
      this.

    • keyValue

      public LogFormatter.Builder keyValue(String key, @Nullable String fallback)
      Creates a formatter that will print a single key's value, Logback/Log4j2 %X{key} style: just the raw value (or the fallback, or an empty string if neither is present) - no key prefix, no percent encoding. For the percent-encoded key=value style instead, see encodedKeyValue(String, String).
      Parameters:
      key - key to select.
      fallback - if the value is null the fallback will be used.
      Returns:
      this.

    • encodedKeyValues

      public LogFormatter.Builder encodedKeyValues()
      Creates a formatter that will print ALL of the key values by percent encoding (RFC 3986 URI aka the format usually used in URI.getQuery()). Keys that are mapped to null will only have the key printed and no separating equal sign (=). This is to differentiate empty string and null - the same behavior as LogFormatter.KeyValueNullStrategy.KEEP. For Logback's %X style instead, see keyValues().
      Returns:
      formatter.

    • encodedKeyValues

      public LogFormatter.Builder encodedKeyValues(List<String> keys)
      Creates a formatter that will print the key values in order of the passed in keys if they exist in percent encoding (RFC 3986 URI aka the format usually used in URI.getQuery()), preserving the null/empty-string distinction for a key whose value is null (LogFormatter.KeyValueNullStrategy.KEEP - most key values, e.g. MDC, are never actually mapped to null in practice, so this only matters if yours are). An empty keys list is a noop - no formatter is added at all. If you want all keys use encodedKeyValues(). For Logback's %X style instead, see keyValues(List).
      Parameters:
      keys - keys where order is important.
      Returns:
      this.
      See Also:
      • encodedKeyValues(List, KeyValueNullStrategy)

    • encodedKeyValues

      public LogFormatter.Builder encodedKeyValues(List<String> keys, LogFormatter.KeyValueNullStrategy nullStrategy)
      Creates a formatter that will print the key values in order of the passed in keys if they exist in percent encoding (RFC 3986 URI aka the format usually used in URI.getQuery()), handling keys whose value is null (or simply absent - the two are indistinguishable, see LogFormatter.KeyValueNullStrategy) according to nullStrategy. An empty keys list is a noop - no formatter is added at all. If you want all keys use encodedKeyValues(). For Logback's %X style instead, see keyValues(List).
      Parameters:
      keys - keys where order is important.
      nullStrategy - how to handle a key whose value is null or absent.
      Returns:
      this.
